newsitem.title: USA: Daschle warns U.S. tax bill talks may drag to Sept.
newsitem.headline: Daschle warns U.S. tax bill talks may drag to Sept.

text.p: Senate Democratic Leader Tom Daschle said the White House and Congress had made no progress in talks on a tax-cut bill, warning talks could drag on into September -- well past the proposed Aug 1 deadline.

Daschle also told reporters it was time for Republicans to make concessions. He warned that Democrats may refuse to compromise further on the bill, calling for a net $85 billion tax cut over five years.
"I think we've given all we can give. I don't know that the president and the Democrats can give any more," Daschle said.

Daschle also warned that negotiations on spending cuts needed to implement a five-year balanced budget deal could drag into September, saying there were a number of controversial Medicare issues still to be resolved.

He said that White House officials told him no progress was made during meetings with Republicans Wednesday on the tax bill. "The meeting was simply a restatement of position that got nowhere," he said.
He said House Republican resistance to a 20-cents-per-pack cigarette tax approved by the Senate was also a problem.
